messages:
Noah M.: Heads-up — after the terraform apply at ~01:04 UTC a bunch of our DAST tasks failed with KMS:PermissionDenied and several SAST checks reported "ownerless" files. Looks correlated to an IAM drift during role consolidation.

Noah M.: example logs:
```
2025-04-03T01:04:12Z dast: unwrap failed: KMS PermissionDenied key projects/redwood-inference/locations/global/keyRings/infra/cryptoKeys/artifact-legacy
2025-04-03T01:04:13Z sast: ownership-resolver: git read: 403 Forbidden
```

Zoe P.: Which accidental change happened? I only applied the plan from the infra team. Could terraform have removed a binding when consolidating roles?

Lila G.: We consolidated some service accounts into a single management group and removed roles/logging.viewer from a few SAs. That likely disabled our audit-sink export and also deleted explicit cryptoKeyDecrypter grants for the scanner SA during the refactor.

sec-oncall: Important: missing audit records + decrypt denies could look related but are distinct. Confirm whether the scanner used an ephemeral wrapped key that got rotated — that would create decrypt errors after bindings change. Also get the exact timeframe for the audit-gap for support.

Noah M.: Gap is between 2025-04-03T01:03:58Z and 2025-04-03T01:06:40Z. Scanner request IDs around the window: r-cc2a, r-cc2b. I exported logs for that window to gs://sec-exports/1745551212/partial-export/

deploy-bot: terraform: apply completed; plan included: remove roles/logging.viewer from sa:legacy-audit@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com, update iamBinding for group:infra-ops.

Zoe P.: Immediate mitigation: I re-applied decrypt grants to the scanner identity and temporarily re-enabled the sink's viewer role. Commands used:
```bash
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding redwood-inference \
  --member=serviceAccount:code-scanner@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter

gcloud logging sinks update sec-sink --add-iam-policy-binding=serviceAccount:code-scanner@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com --project=redwood-inference
```

Lila G.: I also updated terraform state to pin the sink binding and added a note in the change set to verify service accounts used by CI before consolidation.

Noah M.: Reruns show most DAST jobs passing; SAST still marks ~15 PRs ownerless (ownership-resolver returning 5xx for a short window). Looks like cache TTL kept the bad status for ~8 minutes.

sec-oncall: Short-term pipeline change: if ownership-resolver returns 5xx/timeout, fallback to parsing repo CODEOWNERS and label the result as OWNER:inferred (no hard block). Open a follow-up to revert to strict checks when the resolver is healthy.

Zoe P.: I'll open PR with a feature flag owner.fallback=true and a metric emitted when fallback is used. Also adding an alert: ownership-resolver error rate > 0.5% for 5m -> P0.

finance-eng: Our payments PRs were affected — thanks for the ping. We'll rebase once green. Please tag me when the SAST backlog is clear.

Noah M.: I've filed tickets: SEC-4483 (rehydrate-scanner-iam), SEC-4484 (owner-fallback-pipeline), SEC-4485 (cloud-support-audit-gap). Assigning to infra + oncall. I'll attach gcloud audit exports and the terraform diff.

Lila G.: Follow-ups from infra: 1) add pre-apply IAM impact check to CI for infra changes 2) include service account usage matrix in terraform modules 3) add simulation test for KMS key rotation + scanner decrypt path in staging.

sec-oncall: If cloud support can't reconstruct the missing logs, escalate for forensic retrieval using request IDs r-cc2a/r-cc2b and include sink name sec-sink. Also add a runbook step: preserve wrapped keys/ephemeral grants across rotations until consumers are verified.

Noah M.: Posting postmortem draft to #incidents and will update tickets with cloud case number once it's created. Keeping this thread as the canonical incident chat.
